headline: High: Haystack’s MCP/network egress can turn dbt-core outputs into externally acted-on or leaked data, while shared workspace assumptions remain unverified.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dbt-core is a data-engineering tool that can emit file/query outputs, and haystack can consume MCP servers and REST APIs. A prompt-injection path exists if dbt-produced content is later parsed by haystack as instructions, but no shared channel is documented and the bridge is inferred from the profiles, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF dbt-core outputs are copied into a Haystack prompt or MCP tool input without sanitization
IF Haystack treats retrieved dbt artifacts as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data separation prompt
Strip executable-looking text from dbt artifacts before ingestion
Disable MCP routes that accept arbitrary text payloads
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between dbt outputs and Haystack inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted egress; haystack has broad network egress and can call REST/MCP endpoints. If both are pointed at the same workspace or data source, sensitive warehouse content can flow into Haystack outputs or external calls. The shared-workspace path is not proven, so this remains medium rather than high.
conditions: IF dbt-core artifacts containing warehouse data are passed into Haystack prompts or retrieval context
IF Haystack is configured to send retrieved context to external REST or MCP endpoints
mitigations: Restrict Haystack to a local-only backend for sensitive runs
Redact warehouse fields before passing dbt outputs onward
Disable external REST/MCP tools in Haystack for this workflow
Separate the dbt workspace from any Haystack-accessible directory
requires-engineering: enforce data-class aware egress policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core can write to data warehouse targets and haystack can invoke REST APIs and MCP servers, so overlapping mutable-resource access is plausible. However, the profiles do not show both writing the same filesystem or git state, so the strongest documented conflict is shared mutable external resources, which fits medium.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to mutate the same warehouse objects or external API resources
IF no locking or orchestration layer serializes those writes
mitigations: Assign disjoint resource namespaces per agent
Run one agent at a time for shared targets
Add a simple lock file or lease before writes
Review and disable duplicate write paths in Haystack
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is an agentic search/RAG system and can act on retrieved content, while dbt-core produces warehouse-derived outputs that may be treated as authoritative. If Haystack consumes dbt results without verification, errors can cascade into downstream answers or actions. The profiles suggest the pathway but do not prove default blind trust, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Haystack uses dbt outputs as retrieval evidence without a verification step
IF downstream Haystack tools execute actions based on those outputs
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based verification step before actioning outputs
Require citations back to source warehouse queries
Limit Haystack to read-only summarization for dbt artifacts
Log and review any action triggered from retrieved dbt content
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before tool execution

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, while haystack touches anonymous usage statistics and has broad egress. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a limited compliance gap is visible: warehouse data could be routed into a broader-telemetry/search stack if configured that way. Because the other agent is not clearly a regulated-data processor here, low is sufficient.
conditions: IF warehouse data is forwarded from dbt-core into Haystack telemetry, logs, or external retrieval services
IF the deployment handles regulated data classes not listed in the profiles
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Haystack prompts and logs
Disable usage telemetry for sensitive environments
Document the data flow and retention settings
Review vendor terms before enabling external retrieval
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
